title: Seasonal shares gave no clear timing-gap change at Ob and Lena in matched certified years from 1980 to 2011
abstract: We tested whether seasonal flow shares explain a change in the annual-minus-spring flow midpoint gap at Ob and Lena. We used ArcticGRO v20261104 and 31 common certified years in 1980-2011, excluding 2000. An exact two-factor decomposition compared equal-year flow curves in 1980-1995 and 1996-2011. Share contributions were 2.14 days for Ob and 2.85 days for Lena, with 97.5% five-year block limits of -1.90 to 6.18 and -1.04 to 6.51 days. Thus neither primary test gave a clear positive share effect. Matched-period Yenisey evidence was also uncertain. Most checks kept this result, but an April-August spring window gave a positive Lena interval. Short records, season choice, regulation and conditional uncertainty limit the finding. The decomposition does not identify a physical cause. Code, aggregate evidence, hashes, a numerical audit and a figure are included; source records stay external.

display.caption: Timing-gap changes and seasonal-share and daily-shape contributions in 31 matched certified years. Bars show 97.5% marginal five-year block limits. The two primary tests are the Ob and Lena share terms.
